data.why: A red car on a garage driveway, cut away low so its air bags show, with the air kit building up beside it in the order the air flows: compressor, tank, valve, water trap, a valve per bag, nylon lines, height sensors, shock absorbers and a remote. A big ball lies under the car: the leaking car sags onto it, the low car scrapes it, and the finished car lifts off it. Shots frame the car (and the kit when a kit part arrives), close on the bags.

recurring.what: a big ball under the car: sagged on, scraped, and finally cleared

ideas.idea: If you swap steel springs for bags of air, you have air suspension
a bag leaks, and the car sags onto a ball
you add a compressor that pumps air back in
the slow pump lets the car sink after every bump
you add a tank that refills it in seconds
the tank's air rushes in, and the car shoots up
a valve lets air in or out
This is an air spring
each time the valve opens, water drips out
a water trap catches it first
with water trapped, a heavy trunk tips it back
each bag gets its own valve to level it
four valves need four long lines, and they leak
you clip tough nylon lines along the frame
low on its lines, the car scrapes the ball
height sensors at each corner lift it up
lifted high on the highway, the car sways
the sensors lower it as you speed up
lowered over a pothole, it bounces on and on
you add shock absorbers that stop the bouncing
parked overnight, slow leaks sink it while the shocks sit
a remote button pumps it back up
Press the button, and your bags of air lift it off the ball
Congratulations, you built a bagged car

chain.stakes: the headlights point at the sky

chain.shows: air sprays from the long lines
the low car scrapes the ball

chain.stakes: it rolls in the wind and the turns

chain.shows: the lowered car bounces on and on

chain.stakes: it sits on the ground by morning

surprises.claim: Air suspension systems use a compressor to fill an air tank, which then fills the air springs through valves.
surprises.search: air suspension compressor tank valves air springs how it works

surprises.claim: Compressed air holds moisture that condenses as water in the air tank, so air ride systems use water traps or drains.
surprises.search: air ride suspension water trap moisture tank drain

surprises.claim: Many air suspension systems use height sensors at each corner and can lower the car automatically at highway speed.
surprises.search: air suspension height sensors lowers automatically highway speed

surprises.claim: Air suspension still needs shock absorbers to stop the car from bouncing.
surprises.search: air suspension needs shock absorbers air springs bounce damping

sentences.text: If you swap steel springs for bags of air, you have air suspension.
But a bag leaks, and the car sags onto a ball.
So you add a compressor that pumps air back in.
But the slow pump lets the car sink after every bump.
So you add a tank that refills it in seconds.
But the tank's air rushes in, and the car shoots up.
So a valve lets air in or out.
This is an air spring.
But each time the valve opens, water drips out.
So a water trap catches it first.
But with water trapped, a heavy trunk tips it back.
So each bag gets its own valve to level it.
But four valves need four long lines, and they leak.
So you clip tough nylon lines along the frame.
But low on its lines, the car scrapes the ball.
So height sensors at each corner lift it up.
But lifted high on the highway, the car sways.
So the sensors lower it as you speed up.
But lowered over a pothole, it bounces on and on.
So you add shock absorbers that stop the bouncing.
But parked overnight, slow leaks sink it while the shocks sit.
So a remote button pumps it back up.
Press the button, and your bags of air lift it off the ball.
Congratulations, you built a bagged car.
